historical_references.reference: Benedetta Borghi (1386-1463) was a Bolognese nun and mystic who experienced a series of visions and ecstatic experiences. Her writings, which detail her visions and the teachings she received, were widely read and influential in the late Middle Ages. Benedetta's experiences were characterized by a strong sense of union with Christ and a focus on the Passion. She was also known for her devotion to the Eucharist.

Benedetta Carlini (1526-1566) was a lay sister in the Tuscan Benedictine monastery of Monte Oliveto Maggiore. She was known for her mystical experiences and visions, which were characterized by a deep connection to the natural world and a strong sense of feminine spirituality. Her writings, which were influenced by the works of Teresa of Avila and Catherine of Siena, were influential in the Counter-Reformation period.
